questions.question: Are Razorpay and Meta inbound webhooks idempotent against provider-side retries, and do they correctly avoid retry storms on unroutable events?
questions.why_it_matters: Razorpay/Meta retry non-2xx responses; a webhook that throws on an unresolvable-but-valid event (e.g. a payload the product doesn't recognize) can be retried forever and can even get the webhook URL disabled by the provider, breaking ALL future crediting.
questions.answer: Yes, with real prior-incident scarring visible in the code comments. RazorpayWebhookController: `payment.captured` is deliberately routed through a nullable-receipt-tolerant path (dispatchFundingEventIfResolvable) specifically because an earlier version threw ESCROW_NOT_FOUND on a receipt-less payload and caused an infinite Razorpay retry storm (documented inline, referencing a fixed defect). Unknown event types hit a no-op `default` branch returning 200 (never a throw), and events belonging to the same Razorpay account's OTHER product (Snapsby, a shared account per F-0809) are caught narrowly by TOPUP_NOT_FOUND/ESCROW_NOT_FOUND only and ACKed rather than retried forever. Idempotency: subscription.* events go through IdempotencyService.executeOnce keyed on eventType+subscriptionId+webhook created_at (survives Razorpay's own retries of the identical delivery); order.paid/payment.captured funding events rely on EscrowService.confirmFunded's own status check (`if (hold.getStatus()==FUNDED) return hold;` inside an actual @Transactional method) as their idempotency layer instead — a second, different mechanism, but a functioning one. Meta's compliance callbacks (MetaPlatformCallbackController) similarly HMAC-verify the signed_request before parsing and use their own IdempotencyService scope (meta.platform.callback).
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/razorpay/RazorpayWebhookController.java lines 89-157 (switch dispatch, inline comments naming the [B11/H-8] retry-storm fix and F-0809 shared-account narrowing), lines 310-345 (subscription idempotency via IdempotencyService); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/EscrowService.java lines 451-462 (confirmFunded's own-status idempotent no-op, @Transactional at line 450); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/meta/webhook/MetaPlatformCallbackController.java (HMAC verify-before-parse, CALLBACK_IDEMPOTENCY_SCOPE).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Static/code-level only — no live Razorpay/Meta sandbox delivery was replayed in this audit (out of scope, read-only). RazorpayWebhookControllerTest exists (confirmed on disk) which raises confidence this is exercised by tests, but its actual pass/fail was not re-run here.

questions.question: Does the codebase have any circuit-breaker, bulkhead, or standardized retry library protecting outbound calls to Razorpay/Meta/MSG91/third-party AI, and are HTTP timeouts consistently configured?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a circuit breaker or timeout, one degraded external dependency can hang worker/scheduler threads indefinitely, cascading into unrelated jobs (the exact failure class TaskSchedulerConfig's own javadoc describes for a different cause).

Timeout coverage is inconsistent: SMTP (used by Msg91EmailClient/EmailWorker) has explicit 10s connect/read/write timeouts in application.yml (`spring.mail.properties.mail.smtp.{connectiontimeout,timeout,writetimeout}: 10000`). By contrast, MetaGraphApiClient.java — the single shared HTTP client underlying InstagramInsightsClient, FacebookPageClient, MetricsPollingJob, AudienceDemographicsJob, CreatorCaptionSyncJob, MetaTokenRefreshService — builds its Spring RestClient with only `.baseUrl(...)` and a default JSON Accept header; no `.requestFactory(...)`/connectTimeout/readTimeout call exists anywhere in that file or its callers, so it runs on the JDK HttpClient's own defaults (no read timeout by default). RazorpayClient.java (wrapping the razorpay-java SDK's Order/Plan/Subscription calls) likewise has no visible timeout override in this codebase.

questions.question: What happens when an async event handler (e.g. NotificationListener's @Async @TransactionalEventListener methods, or OtpEmailDispatcher) throws — is there any custom failure handling, retry, or dead-letter, or does it just vanish?
questions.why_it_matters: NotificationListener fans out ~25+ domain events (escrow funded, contract signed, payout released, KYC approved, etc.) to email/notification sends; a silent failure here means a user-facing communication is dropped with no operational signal.
questions.answer: No custom async-failure handling exists. A repo-wide grep for AsyncConfigurer, a custom getAsyncExecutor() override, or AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler returns zero implementations — only `@EnableAsync` on InfluoraApiApplication.java and comments referencing it. Spring's default behavior for a `void`-returning `@Async` method that throws is to hand the exception to `SimpleAsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler`, which only logs it (stack trace to the application log) — there is no retry, no dead-letter row, and no alert/metric emitted for a failed NotificationListener handler. OtpEmailExecutorConfig (a separate, deliberately-isolated executor for OTP mail) does at least use an AbortPolicy with the rejection caught at the call site — but that only covers queue-saturation, not an exception thrown mid-send.
questions.evidence: `grep -rn "AsyncConfigurer\|@EnableAsync\|getAsyncExecutor\|AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler" influora-api/src/main/java` returned only the `@EnableAsync` annotation itself and prose comments referencing it, no implementing class; influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/notification/NotificationListener.java (25+ `@Async @TransactionalEventListener` methods, no per-method try/catch-with-alert visible in the imports/structure reviewed); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/config/OtpEmailExecutorConfig.java (AbortPolicy, documented as deliberate for a different failure mode — queue saturation, not exception-during-send).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not read every one of NotificationListener's 25+ handler method bodies individually to confirm NONE of them has an internal try/catch that logs-and-continues gracefully (some individual handlers may degrade more gracefully than the class-wide default) — this is a class-level architectural observation (no shared safety net), not a proof that every single handler is unguarded.

questions.question: Is there crash-recovery for money-moving jobs that could leave a debit orphaned if the process dies mid-operation (e.g. between debiting a creator wallet and confirming a RazorpayX payout)?
questions.why_it_matters: A crash between 'debit committed' and 'gateway call confirmed' is a classic money-loss/stuck-money bug class; the audit specifically calls out idempotency/failure-recovery/dead-letter handling as in scope.
questions.answer: Yes — this is explicitly designed for and documented as fixing a real prior incident. PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob sweeps Payout rows stuck in STATUS_PENDING longer than a grace period (both the original queue-time debit window AND, per a documented 'Red-team F2' follow-up, the separate admin-retry-path debit window that the original sweep missed), delegating actual resolution to PayoutReconciliationService's reconcileOrphanedPendingPayout/reconcileFailedPayoutRetry. A parallel job, IdempotencyReservationReaperJob, reaps any idempotency_keys row stuck IN_PROGRESS (e.g. a hard kill between reservation-commit and action-completion) by flipping it to FAILED — never COMPLETED, since the job can't know the true outcome — which then feeds the existing reclaimFailedForRetry path rather than permanently blocking the same key. Both jobs follow the same documented pattern: AtomicBoolean single-flight guard, grace-period query (never races a still-legitimately-running instance), and per-row try/catch so one bad row doesn't abort the sweep.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/job/PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob.java (full class javadoc naming the crash window, the queue-time AND admin-retry-path variants, and 'Red-team F2 fix'); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/job/IdempotencyReservationReaperJob.java (STALE_IN_PROGRESS_GRACE_PERIOD = 15 minutes, javadoc naming 'Red-team F2 fix — stale IN_PROGRESS idempotency reservation reaper').
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Did not trace into PayoutReconciliationService.reconcileOrphanedPendingPayout/reconcileFailedPayoutRetry bodies to verify their actual resolution logic (retry vs. reverse) is itself correct — only confirmed the sweep/detection layer exists and is scheduled+locked.

questions.question: Is Meta integration connected via a real-time inbound webhook (e.g. Instagram comments/mentions/messages), or purely a polling model, and what IS webhook-shaped on the Meta side?
questions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly asks to characterize every inbound webhook; conflating 'has a /webhooks/meta path' with 'subscribes to Meta's real-time Webhooks product' would misrepresent the integration.
questions.answer: Purely polling for content/metrics data; the only real Meta-facing webhook endpoints are compliance callbacks, not content webhooks. MetricsPollingJob (a @Scheduled job) pulls Instagram Insights on a schedule via MetaGraphApiClient's synchronous GET calls. /webhooks/meta (MetaPlatformCallbackController) implements only the Deauthorize Callback and Data Deletion Callback that Meta's App Review requires — both are inbound POSTs from Meta, HMAC (signed_request) verified, but they exist to learn about a user revoking consent, not to receive comments/DMs/mentions in real time. A repo-wide grep for `hub.challenge`/`hub.verify_token`/`X-Hub-Signature` (the standard Meta real-time-Webhooks handshake/verification artifacts) returns zero matches anywhere in influora-api/src/main/java — confirming no subscription to Meta's actual Webhooks product exists.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/job/MetricsPollingJob.java (class javadoc: 'Polls Instagram metrics... Phase 2 Data Pipeline'); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/meta/webhook/MetaPlatformCallbackController.java (class javadoc explicitly scoping itself to 'Deauthorize Callback and... Data Deletion Callback'); `grep -rn "hub.challenge\|hub.verify_token\|X-Hub-Signature" influora-api/src/main/java` = no matches.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: This appears to be an intentional architecture choice (polling is simpler and Meta's real-time Webhooks product requires additional App Review scopes), not necessarily a defect — flagged here purely for completeness of the webhook inventory the task asked for.

findings.title: No circuit-breaker/bulkhead library anywhere in the codebase; MetaGraphApiClient's shared RestClient has no explicit connect/read timeout
findings.evidence: `grep -rli "circuitbreaker\|resilience4j\|@Retry\b" influora-api/src/main/java influora-api/pom.xml` = no matches; influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/meta/client/MetaGraphApiClient.java lines 60-75: `RestClient.builder().baseUrl(baseUrlFor(path) + "/" + props.getGraphApiVersion()).defaultHeader(HttpHeaders.ACCEPT, MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE).build()` — no `.requestFactory(...)` or timeout configuration anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: MetricsPollingJob, AudienceDemographicsJob, CreatorCaptionSyncJob, and MetaTokenRefreshService all funnel through this one client. A slow/hanging Meta Graph API response (rate-limit soft-hangs, network partition) has no read-timeout ceiling and no circuit breaker to fail fast on repeated failures — worst case a scheduler-pool thread (of only 10 total, shared across every other job per TaskSchedulerConfig) sits blocked for as long as the OS-level TCP timeout, degrading unrelated scheduled jobs.
findings.recommended_fix: Add explicit connectTimeout/readTimeout to the RestClient's underlying ClientHttpRequestFactory (e.g. via `.requestFactory(ClientHttpRequestFactories.get(...))` with a bounded Duration), and consider a resilience4j CircuitBreaker/TimeLimiter around Meta and Razorpay calls given the shared, limited scheduler thread pool.
findings.verification_required: Runtime reproduction: point MetaApiProperties at a host that accepts a connection but never responds, and time how long a MetricsPollingJob run blocks.

findings.title: No custom async-exception handling for NotificationListener's ~25 @Async event handlers — a thrown exception is only logged by Spring's default handler, with no retry or dead-letter
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "AsyncConfigurer\|getAsyncExecutor\|AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler" influora-api/src/main/java` returns no implementing class, only the bare `@EnableAsync` on InfluoraApiApplication.java:133; influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/notification/NotificationListener.java has ~25 `@Async`-annotated `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` handler methods (import list alone spans AuthOtpEvent through WalletLowBalanceEvent).
findings.impact: A transient failure inside any one of these ~25 handlers (e.g. a DB blip while resolving a recipient, an NPE on an unexpected payload shape) is swallowed after being logged — the triggering event (escrow funded, contract signed, KYC approved, payout released, etc.) never gets its user-facing notification, with no queue-based retry and no operational alert distinct from combing through application logs.
findings.recommended_fix: Register a custom AsyncConfigurer with an AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler that at minimum emits a structured/alertable log or metric per (event type, exception), and evaluate whether business-critical notification events (payout released, KYC approved) should route through the existing EmailOutbox durable-retry pattern instead of a bare @Async fire-and-forget.
findings.verification_required: Force an exception inside one NotificationListener handler in a test/staging environment and confirm no retry occurs and no alert fires beyond a log line.
affected_features: All ~25 domain-event-driven notifications (escrow funded, contract signed, payout released, KYC approved/rejected, subscription halted, etc.)

findings.title: EmailWorker has one self-documented duplicate-send window under simultaneous degraded-SMTP + multi-instance conditions
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/notification/EmailWorker.java class javadoc, section 'Known gap in that guarantee, under degraded SMTP': states a single row taking longer than ~30s can push a batch past its own CLAIM_LEASE (3 minutes), making the row visible to findPendingForSend again so 'another instance may re-claim and re-send it', explicitly scoped to marketing email only, never OTP.
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/notification/EmailWorker.java (class javadoc, 'Known gap' section, near end of file header)
findings.impact: Under a specific, narrow combination (degraded SMTP relay taking >30s per message AND multiple app instances AND a poll landing exactly in that window), a single marketing email could be sent twice to the same recipient. Self-scored by the code's own authors as requiring three simultaneous conditions; blast radius explicitly excludes OTP/transactional mail.
findings.recommended_fix: Already tracked in the code comment as 'tracked, not done here' — deriving the wall-clock deadline from the lease instant itself (rather than from after the claim transaction commits) and reserving margin for the mark transaction would close it, as the comment itself proposes.
findings.verification_required: Would require a live multi-instance deploy against an artificially slow SMTP relay to reproduce — not attempted (out of scope for a read-only audit).

findings.title: WooCommerce webhook flow has no server-side verification that the merchant actually created the webhook correctly — silent breakage risk (design gap, not a code defect)
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/web/WooCommerceConnectController.java class javadoc: 'WooCommerce has no OAuth app-install flow at all: WooCommerce is REST-webhook based... a brand creates a webhook directly in their WordPress admin... and WooCommerce lets them set (or auto-generates) a Secret'; no WooCommerceWebhookRegistrar-equivalent class exists (confirmed absent by directory listing of influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/woocommerce/), unlike Shopify's ShopifyWebhookRegistrar.
findings.impact: This is architecturally correct for WooCommerce (it genuinely has no Shopify-style Admin API for webhook subscription), but there is no equivalent of a 'test webhook' or first-delivery health check — a brand can mistype the URL, pick the wrong topic, or never actually save the webhook in wp-admin, and Influora has no way to detect or surface that until (if ever) the brand notices coupon redemptions aren't tracking.
findings.recommended_fix: Consider a lightweight verification UX: e.g. prompt the brand to trigger a test order/webhook and confirm receipt within N minutes of connecting, surfaced in the connect UI, distinct from a code fix to WooCommerceConnectController itself.
findings.verification_required: Confirm with product/Kavya whether this manual-setup risk is an accepted trade-off already, or worth a follow-up.

area.name: Schedulers, webhooks, n8n/Postiz, email/OTP pipelines, external integration clients
area.status: Core money/notification-moving scheduler and webhook infrastructure is well-engineered and heavily self-documented against real prior incidents (ShedLock, outbox pattern, four independent crash-recovery jobs, two-layer webhook idempotency). The TrendSpark trend-ingestion pipeline (both its n8n and Java forms) and Postiz are the two clearly non-functioning/non-existent pieces in this area as shipped in 115f698. No circuit-breaker pattern exists anywhere, and async notification failures have no safety net beyond default logging.
area.main_evidence: Direct reading of ~25 source files (job/*.java, webhook controllers for Razorpay/Meta/Shopify/WooCommerce, IdempotencyService and its reaper, EmailWorker/EmailOutbox, MetaGraphApiClient, TrendIngestProperties/TrendPullJob), cross-checked against application.yml and all three deploy docker-compose files, plus confirming presence/absence of corresponding test files on disk.
area.main_uncertainty: No code in this RC was actually compiled or executed (no Maven/mvn build was run in this environment); all 'IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED' features would need a real `mvn test`/`mvn verify` pass (or a live staging replay of a Razorpay/Meta/Shopify webhook) to move from code-level confidence to VERIFIED WORKING.
area.limitations: graphify-out/graph.json did not exist in the RC (only in the uncommitted main tree), so graphify query/path/explain could not be used as the task instructed; this audit relied on direct grep/Read against the RC instead, which is slower but did not block coverage of the requested scope. Time/turn budget did not allow tracing every downstream service body referenced by the jobs read (e.g. PayoutReconciliationService's actual resolution logic, WalletService's affiliate-wallet withdrawal eligibility) — those are named as remaining uncertainties on the relevant questions/findings above rather than asserted either way.
